sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises steeply as the share of the credit limit in use grows, with the largest increase at high utilization.
The number of past delinquencies is the second or third most important driver, and having any delinquency raises the risk of default.
Annual income is also the second or third most important driver, and higher income lowers the risk of default, with most of the drop coming between the lower and middle income bands.
Length of credit history has a weak to moderate effect, with longer histories associated with lower risk.
Utilization and credit history do not interact in any way the data can detect.
The data do not settle whether debt-to-income ratio has a weak effect on default risk, since no movement in its curve is resolved at this sample size.
Number of recent credit inquiries and applicant age hardly matter for the predictions.
